subject: research/robofab-graspfast
professional: a robotics researcher in grasp mechanics and contact simulation (MuJoCo user), who would first check that the analytic friction bound is derived for the right load case, that the simulated 'minimum force' is not an artefact of the slip criterion, bisection tolerance, cone type or solver settings, and whether the result adds anything beyond Coulomb friction being reproduced by a Coulomb-friction simulator

evidence.correctness: Ran `python3 experiments/run.py` here (MuJoCo 4.0.0, README says 3.15.0; about 3 min): the 12 'None' cases in Table A are the same 12 (all 400/800 up/side for all three parts), Table B has 39/39 results, the settings sweep and duration check have the same pass/fail pattern. 7 numeric lines differ from the committed results.txt, all by one bisection step (e.g. cover static 0.0586 vs 0.0595 N, ratio 1.00 vs 1.02; link up40 Table B 0.0156 vs 0.0167 N, ratio 0.87 vs 0.94), so the README's quoted 0.89 to 1.02 range becomes 0.87 to 1.01 on the newer MuJoCo: the headline holds, the exact edges are version- and tolerance-dependent. Results restored with git checkout. Independent recomputation: (1) cover mass 1240*40*30*4e-9 = 5.952 g and per-jaw bound at 400 m/s^2 up = 0.005952*(9.81+400)/(2*0.5) = 2.439 N, matching 2.4392; (2) link at 800 up = 0.000357*809.81/(2*0.5) = 0.2892 N, matching; (3) I wrote my own MJCF (own box, own pads, own motion code, 0.15 s run, pyramidal and elliptic cones, mu 0.5 and 0.8, none of the repo code) and drove the 40x30x4 mm cover: at 0.97x the bound it slips 15 to 44 mm, at 1.03x it holds with 0.5 to 1.0 mm for up400, up800, side800 (both mu), and for a mixed 300 up / 300 side load with the elliptic cone (the pyramidal cone fails there at 1.1x, an inscribed-pyramid artefact, so the author's choice of elliptic cones is right). So the bound, and the claim that it is matched within a few percent with fine settings, are confirmed independently. Also the settings dependence: with the repo's holds() cover up400 fails at every force from 2.5 to 60 N at dt 0.2 ms / solref 0.5 ms and holds from 2.5 N upward at dt 0.05 ms / solref 0.1 ms, so holding is monotone in force and the 'None' is a settings failure as claimed. Weaker point: the 1.00 to 1.01 ratio at high acceleration is largely forced by the 2 mm criterion: over 0.05 s a force deficit f gives slip 0.5*f*a*t^2, so 2 mm tolerates only about 0.4% at 800 m/s^2 and 2.5% at 0.02 s (duration check: 0.98 at 0.02 s); the README's open question about the source of the 1 to 2% is therefore partly answerable, and the ratio near 1 is not independent evidence of anything beyond MuJoCo implementing Coulomb friction.

Table A 39 rows, 27 with a result, ratio 0.96 to 1.02, 12 with none: yes (re-run 0.96 to 1.01, same 12). Table B 39 rows, median 1.00, 0.89 to 1.02: yes in the committed file. Settings sweep (six points) and duration check (four points) present: yes. Cover 2.46 N at 400 up and 4.86 N at 800: yes (2.4609, 4.8633). Link 3 to 17 mN: yes. Links to robofab-graspmove/armaccel exist. The live page https://marisstella.app/research/robofab-graspfast/ was not loaded (proxy), unverified. experiments/figure.png exists but is not referenced in the README. paper/whitepaper.md is an abstract plus pointer to the README (no method, results table or figure): a stub. Candidate 'Next steps' (real armaccel trajectory, compliant pads, other three parts) are honestly listed as not done.
evidence.verification: Ran `python3 -m pytest -q tests`: 6 passed in 0.57 s. Mutations: (1) model.moving_bound hypot(G + a_up, a_side) replaced by G + a_up + a_side (sum instead of resultant): all 6 tests PASS, so the combined-load formula that the 'mix' rows and the README bound statement rely on has no test at all (side-only 800 differs by 0.06%, up-only is identical, and the mixed cases are never tested). (2) force_bound scaled by 0.8: caught by test_bound_reduces_to_static and test_bound_up. (3) sim.holds slip tolerance disp_mm 2.0 -> 200: caught by test_hold_at_400_up_fine_settings and test_default_settings_artefact_at_400. All reverted (git status clean for the subject). Weaknesses: the hold tests use a +-30% band around the bound (1.3x holds, 0.7x fails), so they cannot detect a few-percent bias like the 0.89 to 1.02 claim; no test pins any value from results.txt (the headline table is guarded by nothing but a manual re-run); test_default_settings_artefact_at_400 asserts a simulator artefact, so it can flip with a MuJoCo upgrade (it did not on 4.0.0); test_parts_have_mass is trivial; grasp_options, contact_area, bbox and com have no tests.
evidence.craft: Read model.py, sim.py, run.py, tests, whitepaper. Short and readable, MJCF generated with string formatting. Defects: model.py is a declared copy from robofab-graspmove (and the part list from robofab-selfparts) rather than shared code; model.py has an unused contact_area/grasp_options/com surface beyond what the experiment needs (com is never used here); sim.holds rebuilds the MuJoCo model on every bisection call (about 10 per row), which is why the run takes minutes; `import math` inside moving_bound (model.py:73); run.py opens results files without closing them (run.py:62-63); holds() unpacks the same six keyword arguments through three layers (min_force, holds, mjcf) with duplicated defaults solref=0.0005, dt=0.0002 in three places; simulation timing T_SETTLE is a module constant while t_acc is a parameter; the module docstring in sim.py has a run-on first sentence from the copy; 'worst' tracks only the max displacement, not direction, and uses the centre-of-mass relative to the carrier origin (fine for this set-up); bisection 'tol' is relative 2% so the returned value is the upper bracket, a systematic +0 to +2% bias that is never separated from the ratio (limitations admit it). There is no assertion or check that the mujoco version matches the claimed one.
evidence.claims: Backed: 39/39 and 27/39 case counts, the ratio ranges (committed file), the median, cover 2.46/4.86 N, link mN range, the settings-sweep statement that solref 0.5 ms fails at dt 0.2 and 0.1 ms and solref 0.2 ms passes (re-run reproduced), the duration-independence statement (0.98 at 0.02 s, 1.01 at 0.05/0.10/0.15 s), simulation-only scope, 'only a prescribed constant acceleration, not the arm', the AI-assistance note, MIT, and the honest list that the fine settings were chosen after Table A failed. refs.bib is flagged as copied and not re-verified. Slightly over-strong or unbacked: (1) 'it is the simulator' is supported by the sweep but the mechanism 'contact lag, slip of order a*solref*t' is asserted, not demonstrated here; MuJoCo's own documentation recommends a contact time constant of at least about 2 timesteps and a timeconstant well below the event time, which would be the standard explanation and is not cited. (2) 'the bound is a good prediction at those accelerations' for robofab-armaccel is stated for constant acceleration only and the same sentence says so, acceptable. (3) 'about 1 min' runtime is about 3 min on this machine. (4) Version drift: README gives MuJoCo 3.15.0; the committed numbers do not reproduce to the last digit on 4.0.0 (above). (5) Live page unverified. No fabricated numbers found.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could rerun and extend it (two files, pip install mujoco numpy, tests pass), and the settings-dependence table is a useful warning for anyone running a MuJoCo grasp test at high acceleration. But the scientific content is thin and not new: the bound N >= m*|g+a|/(2 mu) for a two-contact friction grasp is textbook grasp mechanics (Mason, Mechanics of Robotic Manipulation, 2001; Nguyen 1988 force-closure; Murray, Li and Sastry 1994), and a Coulomb-friction simulator reproducing Coulomb friction is expected by construction once the contact is resolved; the only genuinely informative result is that coarse contact settings fail, which MuJoCo's documentation already warns about (solref time constant vs timestep), and that one case set (cover, 6 settings) is the whole evidence. No comparison with an independent simulator (Bullet, Drake, Isaac) or with real friction grasps, no pad compliance, tipping or torque about the grasp axis, only 3 of 6 free parts. Nearest prior work: MuJoCo docs on solref/solimp and Todorov et al. 2012; grasp-stability under acceleration in the pick-and-place literature (e.g. high-speed gripper design papers); not compared. The whitepaper is a stub. Sound, honest, small; well below the publishable bar in research/CLAUDE.md.
evidence.domain: Compared against textbook friction-grasp mechanics (Coulomb, two-finger point-contact with friction, load = m(g + a) in the jaw frame) and MuJoCo practice. Right: the load resultant in the pad plane via hypot of vertical and sideways inertial loads (my elliptic-cone check at 300/300 confirmed it), friction supplied by two contacts (factor 2 mu), elliptic cones plus noslip iterations for a hard-friction test, and the explicit statement that mu, density and the 2 mm criterion are assumed. Departs: a real gripper's holding force depends on pad compliance, finite contact patches (torque about the grasp axis is ignored, the bound itself says so), pad stiffness and the force-control bandwidth of the jaw actuator, none of which are modelled; the actuator here is an ideal constant force and the carrier is position-prescribed with mass 1000 kg, so jaw dynamics at 800 m/s^2 are absent; there is no safety factor and no mixed-load test of the formula in the unit tests. A practitioner would call it a clean sanity check of a simulator setting, not a validation of grasp design at arm accelerations.

defects.what: Combined-load bound has no test: replacing hypot(G + a_up, a_side) with the sum G + a_up + a_side passes all 6 tests, although the mixed-load rows and the README bound statement depend on it

Ratio near 1.00 at high acceleration is largely set by the 2 mm slip criterion (a force deficit f slips 0.5*f*a*t^2, so about 0.4% tolerance at 800 m/s^2 over 0.05 s) plus the 2% upper-bracket bisection; the README lists the source of the 1 to 2% as unknown and the near-unity ratio is presented as validation, but it is close to tautological. Committed values also shift by one bisection step on MuJoCo 4.0.0 (range 0.87 to 1.01 instead of 0.89 to 1.02), and the README pins 3.15.0 without noting it
Whitepaper is an abstract plus pointer to the README; no method, table or figure, and figure.png is not referenced anywhere
Contact-lag explanation is asserted without citing MuJoCo's documented solref/timestep guidance; runtime stated as about 1 min but is about 3 min (model rebuilt on every bisection step)

Hold tests use a +-30% force band and the tests pin no value from results.txt, so a few-percent bias in the simulation would pass; one test asserts a simulator artefact that can flip across MuJoCo versions

verdict: A small, honest, reproducible MuJoCo check. The experiment re-runs here with the same pass/fail pattern (12 failures in Table A, 39/39 in Table B) and numbers within one bisection step of the committed ones, and I confirmed the bound and the 'hold within a few percent' claim with an independent MJCF written from scratch (holds at 1.03x, slips at 0.97x, cover, up/side/mixed, mu 0.5 and 0.8). It does not meet the bar because verification is 2 (the combined-load formula can be replaced by a sum and all 6 tests pass; no test pins the headline table; the hold tests use a +-30% band), the scientific content is textbook friction-grasp mechanics reproduced by a Coulomb-friction simulator with a 2 mm criterion that forces the ratio near 1, the contact-setting finding is already in MuJoCo's guidance, and the whitepaper is a stub. Scores: correctness 3, completeness 3, verification 2, craft 2, claims 3, fitness 2, domain 2.
